text:
avani: Quick thought — proposing a compact binary index for rollout metadata to speed up client resolution and cut storage. Sketch below. TL;DR: move from a monolithic JSON blob per rollout to a tiny index + separate compressed payload store. Thoughts?

mike: Love the idea. Two quick Qs: how do we handle backward compatibility with existing pins? And can clients still do partial fetches without pulling the whole blob? :thinking_face:

avani: Migration plan idea: dual-write for 30 days, read-prefers binary if present, fallback to JSON. Clients fetch the index (usually ~2KB) and then fetch details by id. Partial fetch is supported by storing logically-split diffs inside the blob and providing pointers in the index. Example proto sketch: 

```proto
message RolloutIndexEntry {
  string id = 1; // UUID for lookup
  uint32 schema_version = 2;
  uint32 flags = 3; // bitflags: compressed, encrypted, summary_present
  bytes payload_digest = 4; // sha256 of payload for integrity check
  string summary_json = 5; // small human-readable summary for console
}
```

sasha: Concern: encryption and auditability. Binary blobs need KMS-wrapped keys and versioned signing so we can prove what was rolled out when. Also how will the console show rollouts? We need a readable path.

jordan: We can keep a tiny JSON summary in the index (summary_json) for the Console to render. The big blob stays compressed/encrypted in the payload store. Console reads summary_json and only fetches blob when someone clicks "view full metadata".

ellie: Any perf numbers from a prototype? What's expected client-resolve latency at p95/p99?

avani: Ran a quick dev cluster bench: index lookup ~2ms median, blob fetch ~6ms (same region). Typical rollout metadata shrank ~5x after dedupe + compression. P95 for end-to-end resolution (index+blob) ~15ms with a cold cache, ~4-8ms warm. Will include more thorough benchmarks in the RFC.

kevin: A couple of edge cases: rollbacks and partial-apply semantics. We need idempotent apply semantics and a way to mark tombstones. Also index must carry schema_version and migration hooks so old clients can detect incompatible changes.

infra-bot: deploy-checklist reminder: ensure migration dual-write, backfill job + throttling, metrics dashboard for index hits/misses, and a reversible switch to read-old-json.

mike: Sounds good. Can you draft an RFC with the proto, migration plan, RBAC/KMS decisions, and a console path? I can volunteer to review. :thumbsup:

avani: Will do. Drafting RFC now — will include concrete migration timeline, backfill script, monitoring queries, and fallback playbook. Thanks everyone :rocket:
